items.title: 11.1.3 Domains and Ranges of Cosecant Function (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Is hisse ka aakhri function: cosecant. Achhi khabar yeh hai ke aap ab tak jo seekh chuke hain, us se yeh sabaq khud hi ban jayega. Cosecant sine ka ulta (reciprocal) hai, bilkul jaise secant cosine ka ulta tha. To domain cotangent jaisa aur range secant jaisi aayegi. Aakhir mein kitab chhe ke chhe functions ka ek khulasa table deti hai, jo exam ke liye sona hai.

blocks.alt: Unit circle with centre O at the origin, axes X prime X and Y prime Y. It meets the axes at A(1, 0), B(0, 1), C(minus 1, 0) and D(0, minus 1). The terminal side OP, drawn as an arrow, makes angle theta with OX; P(x, y) is on the circle, M is the foot of the perpendicular PM on OX, OM = x and MP = y.
blocks.caption: Figure 11.1 (repeated from 11.1): unit circle with P(x, y) on the terminal side of θ (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text:
\[\csc\theta = \frac{1}{y},\quad y \ne 0\]
\(\Rightarrow\) terminal side \(\overrightarrow{OP}\) ko \(OX\) ya \(OX'\) (yani \(X\)-axis) par nahin aana chahiye
\[\Rightarrow \theta \ne 0, \pm\pi, \pm 2\pi, \ldots\]
\[\Rightarrow \theta \ne n\pi,\ \text{where } n \in \mathbb{Z}\]
Cosecant function ka domain \(= \mathbb{R} - \{x \mid x = n\pi,\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\}\)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Cosecant sine ka reciprocal hai: \(\csc\theta = \frac{1}{y} = \frac{1}{\sin\theta}\). Is ka denominator \(y\) hai, wahi jo cotangent ka tha (\(\cot\theta = \frac{x}{y}\)). Is liye dono ka domain ek hai: har angle, siwaye un ke jin ki terminal side \(X\)-axis par ho (\(0, \pm\pi, \pm 2\pi, \ldots\)).
Yaad rakhne ka tareeqa: jis function ke denominator mein \(\sin\) (yani \(y\)) ho, woh \(X\)-axis par fail hota hai: cot aur cosec. Yeh dono "sin wale bhai" hain.

Kyun ke \(\csc\theta\) \(-1\) aur \(1\) ke darmiyan wali values ke ilawa har value leta hai,
Cosecant function ki range \(= \mathbb{R} - \{x \mid -1 < x < 1\}\)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Wajah wahi hai jo secant mein thi, bas ab \(x\) ki jagah \(y\) hai. \(y\) zero nahin ho sakta aur \(-1 \le y \le 1\), is liye:
\[0 < y \le 1 \Rightarrow \frac{1}{y} \ge 1\]
\[-1 \le y < 0 \Rightarrow \frac{1}{y} \le -1\]
Yani \(\csc\theta \ge 1\) ya \(\csc\theta \le -1\); range \((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\). Kinaare wali values: \(\csc\frac{\pi}{2} = 1\) aur \(\csc\frac{3\pi}{2} = -1\).

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
\(\theta = \frac{\pi}{6}\) (\(30^{\circ}\)) par \(\sin\theta = \frac{1}{2}\), is liye \(\csc\frac{\pi}{6} = 2 \ge 1\).
\(\theta = -\frac{\pi}{6}\) par \(\sin\theta = -\frac{1}{2}\), is liye \(\csc\left(-\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = -2 \le -1\).
Aur \(\theta = \pi\) par \(\sin\pi = 0\), to \(\csc\pi\) undefined: \(\pi\) domain mein nahin.
Ab kitab ka khulasa. Neeche wala table tamaam trigonometric functions ke domains aur ranges ek jagah dikhata hai:

blocks.caption: Domains and ranges of the trigonometric functions (the book's summary table)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Is table ko ratta lagane ki zaroorat nahin; teen joron (pairs) mein yaad kar lijiye:
1. \(\sin\) aur \(\cos\): koi denominator nahin, is liye domain \(\mathbb{R}\); range \([-1, 1]\).
2. \(\tan\) aur \(\sec\): denominator \(\cos x\), is liye \((2n+1)\frac{\pi}{2}\) nikaal do jahan \(\cos x = 0\).
3. \(\cot\) aur \(\operatorname{cosec}\): denominator \(\sin x\), is liye \(n\pi\) nikaal do jahan \(\sin x = 0\).
Range ke liye: \(\tan\) aur \(\cot\) har real value lete hain; \(\sec\) aur \(\operatorname{cosec}\) har value lete hain siwaye un ke jo \(-1\) aur \(1\) ke bilkul darmiyan hain.
(\(\csc\) aur \(\operatorname{cosec}\) ek hi function ke do naam hain; kitab dono istemal karti hai, ghabraiye mat.)

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Table dekhe baghair batayein: \(y = \sec x\) ka domain kya hai, aur kyun?
Jawab: \(\sec x = \frac{1}{\cos x}\), denominator \(\cos x\) hai, jo \((2n+1)\frac{\pi}{2}\) par zero hota hai. Is liye domain \(\mathbb{R} - \{(2n+1)\frac{\pi}{2}\}\). Agar aap ne yeh khud nikaal liya to table aap ko yaad ho chuka hai!

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Aksar short question aata hai: "\(y = \operatorname{cosec} x\) ka domain aur range likhiye." Dono hisse poore likhiye: domain \(\mathbb{R} - \{n\pi : n \in \mathbb{Z}\}\), range \((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\). Sirf ek likhne se number kat jaate hain.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(\csc\theta = \frac{1}{y}\) ke liye \(y \ne 0\): domain \(\mathbb{R} - \{n\pi : n \in \mathbb{Z}\}\), cotangent jaisa.
2. Cosecant ki range: \((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\), secant jaisi.
3. Table ke teen jore: sin, cos (domain \(\mathbb{R}\); range \([-1, 1]\)); tan, sec (\((2n+1)\frac{\pi}{2}\) nikaalo); cot, cosec (\(n\pi\) nikaalo).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Cosecant ko secant ka domain de dena. Cosecant wahan fail hota hai jahan \(\sin\theta = 0\) (\(n\pi\)), secant wahan jahan \(\cos\theta = 0\) (\((2n+1)\frac{\pi}{2}\)). Bachne ka tareeqa: hamesha fraction likh kar denominator dekhiye.
2. Cosecant ki range \(\mathbb{R} - [-1, 1]\) likhna. Is se \(\pm 1\) bhi nikal jaate hain, jab ke \(\operatorname{cosec}\frac{\pi}{2} = 1\). Sirf open interval \((-1, 1)\) nikalta hai.
3. Union ka nishaan \(\cup\) bhool kar \((-\infty, -1], [1, \infty)\) likh dena. Do alag hisson ko jorne ke liye \(\cup\) zaroori hai.
